title: Wild sentence enders: かい, だい, ぜ, ぞ, さ, から, し
summary: The informal enders you meet in anime and manga: かい, だい, ちょうだい, ぜ, ぞ, さ, plus から and し left hanging.

blocks.text: Real, casual Japanese ends sentences in more ways than ね, よ and な. Here are the common ones outside the walled garden. You cannot learn the exact feel from structure alone, but knowing what each one is makes immersion much easier.
かい, だい, どうだい, ちょうだい

**かい** is a softened, rather folksy version of the question か, often heard from men and older speakers. Plain か at the end of casual speech sounds rough, and that is why かい exists: it is the friendly way to ask.
**だい** is だ + かい, used after nouns and な-adjectives. The set phrase **どうだい** ("how is it?") is widely used.

blocks.jp: そこにいるのは誰だい。

blocks.text: **ちょうだい** is an informal equivalent of ください, added to a て-form.

blocks.jp: ちょっと待ってちょうだい。

blocks.text: **ぜ** and **ぞ** are verbal exclamation marks. They are rough and masculine and you will meet them mostly in anime and manga.
**さ** is gentler and heard in real life from all kinds of people. Do not confuse the ender **さ** with **さあ** at the start of a sentence, a pause for thought.
から and し left hanging
**から** is a conjunction. First the full sentence, with the reason and the result:

blocks.jp: さくらが来ないから、帰ります。
blocks.en: Sakura isn't coming, so I'm going home.

blocks.text: Speakers often stop after から and leave the rest unsaid. Tone decides what is left over: it can soften (an explanation) or harden ("you ought to understand").

blocks.en: Because Sakura isn't coming. (the rest is obvious)

blocks.jp: 自転車に乗るのは禁止ですから。
blocks.en: Because riding a bicycle is not allowed. (Soft if you are explaining, stern if you are insisting.)

blocks.text: **し** lists reasons. The standard use gives two or more:

blocks.jp: 遅くなったし、さくらも来ないし、帰ります。
blocks.en: It has gotten late, and Sakura isn't coming either, so I'm going home.

blocks.text: With one reason, し hints that there are others. That takes the pressure off and sounds friendlier. It can soften even a plain rule, as in 禁止だし ("it's not allowed, you know").

blocks.jp: 遅くなったし、帰ります。
blocks.en: It has gotten late (and other things too), so I'm going home.

rows: question after a noun or な-adjective

items: **かい / だい**: soft, folksy question enders; **どうだい** is very common.
**ちょうだい**: informal ください after a て-form.
**ぜ / ぞ**: rough masculine exclamation marks; **さ** is milder and widely used.
**から / し**: left hanging, they imply more; し hints at other reasons.
